comment: Watermarks for the Supabase word-review pass: every candidate the game recorded
up to `reviewed_through` has been judged, so the next pass only has to look at
rows newer than the latest entry here.
`reviewed_through` is the newest `analytics_events.created_at` that existed when
the pass ran -- the queue query's own horizon -- and is the value to filter on:
The per-word record of each verdict lives in two places: `word_sightings.status`
this repo, src/data/word-rejections.json for a rejection and the provenance
lists in scripts/ for an acceptance.

sources: analytics_events.answer_rejected (658 submissions, 590 distinct, 554 not on the curated list)
notes: Accepted words went to scripts/suggested-words.txt and dictionary.json;
`reoxygenate` also got a score override onto `oxygenate`, since re- + a
common verb is a prefix, not a discovery.
The other four keep the Zipf Datamuse measured for them, recorded in
scripts/datamuse-zipf.txt: caprylate 1.10 (9.75 Mythic), conization 1.80
(8.7 Extremely Rare), inosinate 0.79 (9.92 Legend), uridylate 0.68 (9.93
Legend). Without that tier all four would have fallen to the unattested
sentinel and a flat 10.00 Legend the moment they left the live path.
Rejections went to src/data/word-rejections.json with the fault named
(misspelling, proper noun, abbreviation, obsolete, or judged non-word).
Nonsense strings nobody repeated were left to the generic message rather
than filling the file with one-off typos.

sources: suggested_words (one player suggestion that arrived after the first pass)
notes: `combobulate`, tried three times on puzzle 50 (drop `ate`) and then sent
through the suggestion box. Merriam-Webster has no entry for it, and it was
first recorded as not-a-word on that basis -- wrongly: Wiktionary has it as a
verb labelled `humorous`, with citations from 1915 to 2012, and Wiktionary is
the game's other word source. Accepted, then capped onto `discombobulate`
(9.53 Mythic): dropping `dis-` is not a discovery.
Re-checking the whole pass against Wiktionary caught two more of the same
mistake -- `skateable` and `absconce`, both untagged entries rejected on MW's
silence alone. `skateable` is accepted and folds onto `skate` unaided (5.9
Uncommon). `absconce` was accepted, then withdrawn: it is a real noun, but
nothing attests its *use* -- no corpus, no Datamuse frequency, no MW entry, no
citations on the Wiktionary entry, and not in ESDB/SCOWL 80. Its Google Books
signal is 1.7e-10 and flat since 1800, a thousandth of `sconce` and of `boate`
(which this repo does call obsolete): that is the OCR noise floor, not usage.
So it is below the list's evidence bar rather than obsolete, and it carries the
generic not-a-word message, which claims nothing about the word itself.
MW-unknown alone is not grounds for a rejection. The three that stayed
rejected -- `prismaticism`, `quates`, `weatherical` -- have no Wiktionary
entry either. Misspelling calls Wiktionary confirms outright: `centrifical`,
`condusive`, `testical` (misspelling of), `licentuous` (misconstruction of),
`caligrapher` (alternative form of `calligrapher` -- kept out as a spelling of
another word).
A Wiktionary sweep of all 554 rejected submissions found 54 more words with an
untagged ordinary entry and no game-side explanation: the import in
import-wiktionary-words.py keeps only headwords wordfreq can score, and these
score 0.0. Not accepted here -- 43 of the 54 would land a flat 10.00 Legend,
most of them mechanical forms the engine has no fold for (`unspiced`,
`unmasticated`, `riceballs`, `microcalorie`, `skateless`). Prefix folds (un-,
non-, anti-, de-, re-) and a -less fold come first, or the top of the scale
floods. `absconce` also suggests the bar for that sweep: an entry alone is not
enough, a citation or a measurable frequency is.
